patch.value: The publish-attestation gate misses a publish routed through an unquoted shell variable

value.author: codex
value.text:
author=claude
created_at=now
text=shellScalars indexed only quoted assignments, so a bare NPM=npm was never recorded. expandScalars then left $NPM unresolved, tokenizeCommands saw a program named "$NPM" rather than npm, and the line was not recognised as a publish at all. Because the workflow's own legitimate attested publish still satisfied the non-vacuity guard, auditPublishAttestation returned zero failures and the gate reported a clean pass over a workflow containing an unattested publish. The gate was blind rather than wrong, which is the failure mode that keeps a gate trusted while it is not looking.

Measured behaviourally across the fleet rather than by reading the sources, by importing each repository's own verify-release-publish-attestation.ts and auditing a fixture holding one attested publish plus one variable-routed unattested publish. 12 of 17 repositories returned failures=0: pm-graph, pm-starter, pm-csv, pm-context, pm-web, pm-presets, pm-ts-starter, pm-todos, pm-linear, pm-brief, pm-github and pm-slack-standup. 5 already caught it: pm-jira, pm-beads, pm-ops, pm-slack and pm-gantt-chart.

Fix: shellScalars accepts a third alternative for an unquoted single-word value, matching what pm-jira already carries. The existing guard that refuses to inline a value containing a substitution, backtick, quote or parenthesis is unchanged, so a value that would change how its line parses is still never inlined.

The regression test asserts the audit-level property rather than the map contents, so it fails for the reason the gate exists: with the fix reverted it reports failures=0 where 1 is required. The neighbouring assertion that an unquoted value cannot hold a command encoded the old behaviour as intentional and was updated to match, exactly as pm-jira updated it.

This is the fifth time this class of bypass has been fixed in one vendored copy while the others stayed exposed. The root cause is that the verifier is vendored into every package instead of being consumed from pm-ops; that is tracked in the companion repository as pm-cli-website-bunt.

value.author: claude
value.text:
Bot review on the first round (Greptile P1 x2, Sourcery x2) found that reading scalar assignments out of the raw text indexes bindings the shell never makes. All four were reproduced before fixing:
1. A name defined only in a COMMENT was indexed. `# FLAG=--provenance` followed by `npm publish --access public $FLAG` audited as attested and returned zero failures: an unattested publish borrowed its flag from a comment and passed the gate. This is a bypass, and it pre-dates the unquoted-value change because the quoted form (`# CMD="npm publish"`) was indexed the same way.
2. A name inside a quoted argument was indexed. `echo "config NPM=npm"` bound NPM, so a later literal `$NPM publish` was audited as an npm publish the shell never runs.
3. An unquoted value continuing into an expansion was truncated to its prefix. `NPM=npm$SUFFIX` bound NPM to `npm`; the literal guard then saw no `$` because the `$` had been excluded from the capture, so a value the scan cannot resolve was treated as one it could.
4. The docstring still said only quoted values are indexed.
Fixed by reading assignments from tokenizeCommands instead of from raw text. The tokeniser has already dropped comments and resolved quoting, so a word is only treated as an assignment where the shell would treat it as one; it keeps `$SUFFIX` inside the word, so the literal guard sees the whole value rather than a prefix; and only a command-leading word can assign, so `npm publish FOO=bar` is an argument rather than a binding.
One consequence found by the existing suite rather than by a bot: the tokeniser consumes a substitution instead of keeping its text, so `SUBST="$(node -p 1)"` arrives as an empty value that the literal guard would accept. Inlining it would ERASE `$SUBST` from the command, turning "not understood" into "carries no flags" — the exact false-pass this module already warns about. Empty values are therefore never indexed.
Both new tests were observed failing against the previous implementation and passing after. Verified behaviourally in all 17 packages carrying this file: the comment bypass, the quoted-argument binding, the truncation and the substitution are all refused, while `NPM=npm`, `CMD="npm publish"` and a leading `FOO=bar` still resolve.

value.author: claude
value.text:
Round 3. Greptile raised three further P1 security findings against the tokeniser-based implementation, and all three reproduced:
1. Substitution suffix. `NPM=npm$(printf foo)` — the tokeniser consumes the substitution before the literal guard sees the value, so NPM was bound to the prefix `npm`. The scan then analysed a different command from the one the shell runs.
2. Command-scoped assignment leaked file-wide. `FLAG=--provenance some-command` binds only for that one command, but it was stored in the file-global map, so a LATER `npm publish --access public $FLAG` was rewritten into an attested-looking publish. Audit returned zero failures: a false pass.
3. Subshell escape. `$(FLAG=--provenance)` is a binding the outer shell never sees, but the recursive tokeniser returns the nested command and its assignment was promoted into the outer map. Also a false pass, also measured at zero failures.
Replaced the rule rather than patching three more cases. A name is now taken only from a line that is EXACTLY one assignment carrying a fully literal value, anchored at both ends. Anchoring closes the truncation pair, because a value that does not reach the end of the line is not the value. Requiring the line to hold nothing else closes the comment, quoted-argument, command-scoped and subshell cases in one rule instead of four special cases. Escapes are honoured so `NPM=npm\ publish` still holds a command in one word, which was a Sourcery finding, and the existing refusal of any value carrying a substitution, backtick, quote or parenthesis now applies after unescaping.
`FOO=bar npm publish` is deliberately no longer indexed. It is command-scoped, and the publish on that same line is visible to the scan directly, so nothing is lost.
Verified across all 17 packages carrying this file by exercising 16 properties against each package's own verifier rather than by comparing files. The two regression tests were observed failing against the previous implementation and passing after.
One finding was accepted as valid but deliberately left out of this change: scalars are still resolved from a file-wide map, so a later assignment can rewrite an earlier use. Raised by Sourcery, reproduced, and filed as companion item pm-cli-website-1j4o because it is a different defect needing position-aware resolution.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Baseline reproduction before code changes: built the package with npm run build, initialized a scratch pm project through the installed real CLI, created a synthetic issue, and dispatched the built web status extension through the real SDK testing engine. The staged workflow had an attested sibling plus an unattested path. pm-ops 2026.10.4 rejects PUB="npm publish"; $PUB --access public, but returns zero failures for an enabled alias ship="npm publish" followed by ship --access public and for ship() { npm "$@"; } followed by ship publish --access public. These are live publish paths masked by the attested sibling. Preserve canonical resolution, add fail-closed checks at the consumer boundary, and cover both verdicts where supported; unsupported indirection must fail even with a provenance-looking argument.

value.command: npm run build && npm run build:test && node --test test/publish-indirection.test.ts test/verify-release-publish-attestation.test.ts

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Behavioral revert proof: replaced only auditPublishAttestation with return canonicalAudit(sources), leaving imports, verify, launcher and test files unchanged. The targeted suite loaded and ran 45 tests: 27 passed and 18 failed with assertion failures, including alias and forwarded-function publishing; no module-loading or syntax failures. Restored the exact implementation bytes and reran the complete focused suite. Supplemental checks also reject partial executable substitutions, unknown publish flags, executable arrays and cross-step provenance evidence; supported attested scalar commands, literal functions/evaluators and quoted provenance flags remain accepted. pm test --run --progress passed; automatic test-result persistence is disabled by repository policy, so evidence is recorded in comments.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Canonical convergence is tracked separately as pm-web-vyxu. No changes were made to pm-ops or hosted services. README and docs/publish-attestation.md describe supported syntax, conservative rejections and the canonical change needed.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Default worktree npm release:check ran 534 tests: 523 passed, 11 failed, zero skipped. Three failures are the existing catalog worktree-discovery/snapshot blockers (pm-web-cqwm and pm-web-s99c); eight arise from extensionless CommonJS fixtures inheriting shared scratch ESM metadata. With an isolated CommonJS scratch root the affected 26-test launcher/route subset passes. Will also verify unchanged gates at the committed head in a standalone copy inside the package worktree, matching CI layout; this measures committed snapshot invariants rather than live fleet freshness.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Additional SDK integration observation: initializing a scratch pm tracker underneath an existing Git checkout configures enclosing Git merge attributes for that nested tracker. Tests must initialize their own Git repository first or keep scratch trackers outside checkout ancestry. The new regression helper now initializes Git before pm. Generated scratch merge-attribute additions from validation will be restored to the original tracked file; no SDK API bug was established or filed.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Worktree Bun release:check also executed at unchanged thresholds. With in-checkout scratch storage it ran 492 tests, 483 passed and 9 failed, zero skipped: catalog worktree discovery plus scratch-source visibility, ancestor dependency lookup and explicit-tracker selection. Its measured source metrics were 90.28% statements/lines, 79.50% branches and 93.90% functions, but failed tests invalidate the gate. Scratch storage is now outside Git ancestry with explicit CommonJS metadata; the new helper also sets an explicit fixture pm path before init/create/get. Restored all validation-generated enclosing merge attributes. Standalone validation will retain the same source/test sets and thresholds.
